questions.question: Why correlate findings across multiple tools instead of reporting each tool's output separately?
options: It makes reports longer and more impressive
Correlation deduplicates findings and builds a higher-confidence picture than any single tool provides
Most tools refuse to run alone
Correlation is required by compliance frameworks
questions.explanation: Each tool sees part of the picture. Correlating subdomains, services, screenshots, and metadata across tools removes duplicates, confirms findings, and reveals patterns and anomalies.

questions.question: Who is the audience for an executive summary in an ASM report?
options: Other security engineers who want command output
Non-technical stakeholders who need risk and business impact, not tool details
The tools' developers
External auditors only
questions.explanation: Executive summaries translate technical findings into business risk: what's exposed, what it could cost, and what to do about it — without raw scan output.

questions.question: What makes an ASM finding 'actionable'?
options: It includes a screenshot
It pairs the finding with context and a concrete recommended remediation
It was found by more than one tool
It is rated critical severity
questions.explanation: A list of exposed services isn't actionable by itself. Actionable insights say what was found, why it matters in your environment, and specifically what to do next.

questions.question: What role does data visualization play in ASM analysis?
options: It is purely decorative for reports
It helps spot patterns, trends, and anomalies in large datasets that are hard to see in raw text
It replaces the need for data analysis
It is only useful for executive audiences
questions.explanation: Charts of asset growth, port distributions, or change frequency expose patterns and outliers — like a sudden spike in new subdomains — that scrolling through text output would miss.

questions.question: How should findings be ordered in a professional ASM report?
options: Alphabetically by hostname
In the order the tools produced them
Prioritized by risk and business impact
Grouped by which tool found them
questions.explanation: Reports should lead with what matters most: highest-risk, highest-impact exposures first, so limited remediation time goes where it counts.
